newsitem.title: USA: Albright to visit Russia next week on NATO.
newsitem.headline: Albright to visit Russia next week on NATO.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said Wednesday she would visit Moscow next week to try to work out remaining differences over a proposed NATO-Russia charter.

She told the Senate Armed Services Committee she hoped the alliance would sign such a charter -- to create a formal security cooperation mechanism between NATO and Russia -- in Paris on May 27 but there was no agreement yet.

"I'm going to be going to Moscow to have some additional meetings on the subject, probably next week, because there are elements of the (charter) agreement not decided upon," Albright said. She said no date for the visit had been set.

President Boris Yeltsin and other senior Russian officials have said Moscow would be ready to sign the Russia-NATO charter -- proposed as a way to anchor Russia in Europe and to foster cooperation with the western alliance as it expands -- on May 27.
But U.S. officials have insisted this date is not certain and said Russia's demand for binding guarantees remains a stumbling block.

Albright took a hard line on this issue on Wednesday. "Russia would also like us to make absolute commitments in the (proposed Russia-NATO) charter about the deployment of nuclear and conventional forces on the territory's new members," she told the Senate Armed Services Committee. "But we will not compromise on this issue," she said.
